patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — 8x8 documents a broader use-case set; Slack is narrower/specialist.

8x8 documents a broader use-case set; Slack is narrower/specialist. Choose 8x8 only if your buying job matches “Global UCaaS + contact-centre platform (8x8 Work / X Series) — Work X2 research floor ~$24” rather than Slack's shape. Choose Slack only if your buying job matches “Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Business+ $1” rather than 8x8's shape. Workflow advantage: 8x8 leans business-phone, sales-calling; Slack leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — 8x8 documents a broader use-case set; Slack is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: 8x8 is Global UCaaS + contact-centre platform (8x8 Work / X Series) — Work X2 research floor ~$24/user/month annual; CC tiers custom/higher.; Slack is Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Business+ $15, Enterprise+ contact sales; huddles for light vi.
- Company-size focus: 8x8 (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Slack (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: 8x8-leaning business-phone, sales-calling, contact-center vs Slack-leaning —.
- Researched limits: 8x8 — Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated; Slack — Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer.

Limitations — 8x8: Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated; Mandatory regulatory/service fees frequently sit on top of list seats; Slack: Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer; No SMS or WhatsApp Business customer channels.

Poor-fit cases: 8x8 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated · Slack is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer · Avoid 8x8 if you actually need Slack's motion (Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Bu)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
